evidence: The samples were characterized by means of transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) measurements. The CuPd system was chosen in this study because it is a relatively well-known system in which alloying easily takes place. The formation of a CuPd alloy might be used to improve the selectivity in catalytic reactions such as isomerization and aromatization. In combined X-ray diffraction and theoretical modeling studies on polyvinylpyrrolidone-stabilized CuPd clusters, prepared from a colloidal suspension of acetates, it was found that the nanoparticles exhibit face-dependent surface segregation with surfaces enriched in Cu. A combined XRD and LEIS study showed that an alloy was formed in silica-supported CuPd acetylacetonates clusters after the organic ligands were eliminated under argon flow. The LEIS experiments revealed that the surface of the particles had a higher Cu concentration than the bulk. The measurements were supported by Monte Carlo simulations, employing the modified tight binding method. In a recent XAFS/XRD study in which alumina-supported CuPd catalysts, prepared by coimpregnation of aqueous solutions of PdCl2 and CuCl2, were studied during CO oxidation, no alloying was reported.
